quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

37 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Can you legally cross a double solid yellow line to pass another car?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Only if there is no oncoming traffic.
Only if the car ahead is driving below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no driver can cross them, except to turn into a driveway or business entrance. Passing over a solid yellow line is never allowed.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Honk at the incoming traffic.
Always keep your current speed.
Speed up to prevent traffic buildup.
Move to another lane if it is safe to let traffic merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if it is safe to let traffic merge.
questions.explanation: On roads with two or more lanes, make room for vehicles entering. If the lane next to you is empty, move over to let them in.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, wait for a clear road ahead and slowly reduce your speed to encourage them to pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If a car is tailgating you and a right lane is open, move to it. If no right lane exists, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slowly reduce speed to let them pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the chance of being hit from behind.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When traveling through an intersection.
When passing a bicycle rider.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others who may not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an animal on the road?

options.text: No special action is needed.
Honk your horn.
Pass as close to it as possible.
Be very careful and cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very careful and cautious.
questions.explanation: Always be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: What happens when you mix drugs with alcohol?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It makes alcohol less harmful.
It does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (including prescription and over-the-counter medicines) can hurt your brain function and driving safety. Mixing drugs with alcohol greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
You can drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when visibility is reduced to 500 feet or less. Set them to low beam. High beams in fog reflect light back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Your license will be suspended if you are convicted of:

options.text: Driving without a license.
Passing a stopped school bus.
Failing to yield the right-of-way.
Driving faster than 75 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving faster than 75 mph.
questions.explanation: The DMV can suspend your license for driving faster than 75 mph. Other violations like passing a school bus or failing to yield add points. If you get too many points, your license can be suspended.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow to the speed shown.
A divided highway is starting. Slow to the speed shown.
You need to merge. Slow to the speed shown.
The road winds ahead. Slow to the speed shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow to the speed shown.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves to the right. Drivers should slow down to the safe speed listed on the sign (in this case, 35 mph).

questions.question: How many points are added to your license for passing a stopped school bus?

options.text: One point
Two points
Four points
Five points

questions.correctAnswerText: Five points
questions.explanation: In North Carolina, passing a stopped school bus adds five points to your driving record. Aggressive driving also adds five points.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.
Watch for drunk drivers.
A dangerous curve is ahead.
A bump in the road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells drivers to be careful when the road is wet because it may be slippery and hard to control.

questions.question: You had an upsetting incident at work. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly to stop thinking about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to release your anger.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset, angry, or distracted, wait before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
A traffic signal is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
A school crossing is ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic on a green light must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that when turning left on a green light, they must wait for oncoming traffic to pass first.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.
Not turn on any vehicle lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an approaching vehicle and within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, a driver must:

options.text: Not stop.
Slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where they can see at least 200 feet on each side, even if they enter the intersecting roadway.
Stop where they can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where they can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Without a stop line or crosswalk, stop at the point closest to the intersecting roadway where you can see oncoming traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Faster driving makes your tires less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slower driving makes the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Faster driving makes your tires less effective.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster on wet roads, your tires cannot remove water from the road surface as well. If you go too fast, your tires will lose grip and you will hydroplane (slide on water).

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. You must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes to avoid driving next to the emergency vehicle.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to quickly pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes to avoid driving next to the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. If changing lanes is unsafe or impossible, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always be ready to stop near an emergency scene.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, you should first:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the front car of your desired parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the front car of your desired parking space.
questions.explanation: After checking traffic and signaling, stop parallel to the car in front of your parking space before turning your wheels to park.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.
Trucks are on the upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill or downgrade is coming.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Curve.
Turn right or left.
Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A one-way sign shows that traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means you must slow down as you approach the intersection. You must yield to vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection. Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question:
Which statement about pedestrian deaths is correct?
    I. In cities, two of every five people killed in traffic crashes are pedestrians.
    II. Most pedestrians killed in traffic crashes are teenagers.

options.text: I only
II only
Both I & II
Neither I nor II

questions.correctAnswerText: I only
questions.explanation: In cities, about two of every five people killed in traffic crashes are pedestrians. In rural areas, about one in 10 deaths are pedestrians.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, you:

options.text: May not exit the freeway.
May either continue through the interchange or exit the freeway from your current lane.
May stay in your lane and continue through the interchange.
Must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means this lane will exit the freeway. You cannot stay in this lane and go through the interchange. You must change lanes to continue on the freeway, or you must exit.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane use control signal mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down over a traffic lane means you may use that lane.

questions.question: What happens if you refuse to take a chemical test when an officer asks?

options.text: No negative consequences.
Probation.
A legal settlement.
License revocation.

questions.correctAnswerText: License revocation.
questions.explanation: If you refuse a chemical test, your driver's license will be suspended for at least 30 days. The DMV will also revoke your license for at least 12 months.

questions.question: How should you prepare for anything on the road ahead?

options.text: Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
Maintain focus toward the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.
questions.explanation: You need to find problems before you reach them. Look far ahead, but also scan both sides of the road. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.
Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
Signal to the emergency vehicle when it is clear for them to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.
questions.explanation: You must give emergency vehicles a clear path. If it is safe, pull your vehicle to the side of the road to let them pass.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians and frighten them so they'll think twice before crossing against a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in the intersection, even if you have a green light. Their safety is more important than your right-of-way.

questions.question: What safety restraints work best in a traffic crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags with safety belts provide extra protection in front-end crashes. Use both shoulder and lap belts together.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. What should you do?

options.text: Don't worry about it because all vehicles work the same way.
Hide from your friend that you don't know the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious problems so your friend doesn't feel bad.
Spend a few minutes learning where the controls are and how they work before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes learning where the controls are and how they work before you drive.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take time to learn where the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn are located. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle in a small car, you should be ready for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Extra air pollution.
Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling parts from the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push small vehicles sideways. When passing a large vehicle, be ready to steer to stay in your lane, especially at high speeds.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Drive slower on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water and puddles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car needs more distance to stop and may skid when turning. Don't use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." This means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next sign.
You have time to slow down before entering the slower zone.
You should only go 35 mph if the weather is bad.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A "Reduced speed" sign tells you to slow down. The new speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about road conditions and dangers ahead. This sign tells you that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. How should you merge into traffic?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Use the on-ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Let traffic already on the freeway go first.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to freeway speed and let traffic already on the freeway pass first. Check your mirrors and blind spots before you merge to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: A divided highway is starting.
A steep hill is ahead.
The overpass ahead is not very tall.
Two lanes of opposite traffic are about to join.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead is not very tall.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not drive under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (such as 13 feet, 6 inches).
